review.title: Giving or lending the commonwealth's credit
review.plain: Replaces Section 1 of Article LXII: the commonwealth may give, loan or pledge its credit only by a two-thirds yea-and-nay vote of each house of the general court, and its credit shall not be given or loaned to any individual, private association or privately owned and managed corporation.
powers: The commonwealth may give, loan or pledge its credit
limits: only by a vote, taken by the yeas and nays, of two-thirds of each house of the general court present and voting thereon
The credit of the commonwealth shall not in any manner be given or loaned to or in aid of any individual

provisions.what: Article LXII of the Amendments to the Constitution is hereby amended by striking out section 1 and inserting in place thereof the following section
The commonwealth may give, loan or pledge its credit only by a vote, taken by the yeas and nays, of two-thirds of each house of the general court present and voting thereon
requires: a vote, taken by the yeas and nays, of two-thirds of each house of the general court present and voting thereon

provisions.what: The credit of the commonwealth shall not in any manner be given or loaned to or in aid of any individual, or of any private association, or of any corporation which is privately owned and managed
forbids: Giving or loaning the credit of the commonwealth to or in aid of any individual, or of any private association, or of any corporation which is privately owned and managed

review.title: Opinions of the justices
review.plain: Replaces Article II of Chapter III: each branch of the legislature, and the governor or the council, may require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court upon important questions of law and upon solemn occasions.
powers: shall have authority to require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court

provisions.what: Article II of Chapter III of the constitution of the commonwealth is hereby annulled and the following is adopted in place thereof

Each branch of the legislature, as well as the governor or the council, shall have authority to require the opinions of the justices of the supreme judicial court, upon important questions of law, and upon solemn occasions
provisions.holder: Each branch of the legislature, the governor or the council
provisions.binds: The justices of the supreme judicial court
conditions: upon important questions of law, and upon solemn occasions

review.title: Governor and lieutenant-governor voted on as a group
review.plain: Party candidates for governor and lieutenant-governor are grouped on the state election ballot by party; a voter may cast a single vote for a group, counting for each candidate in it, but may not vote for only one of them.
rights: the voter may cast a single vote for any such group
limits: may not cast a vote for only one of the candidates in such group

provisions.what: Names of candidates of political parties for the offices of governor and lieutenant-governor shall be grouped on the official ballot for use at state elections according to the parties they represent
the voter may cast a single vote for any such group, which shall count as a vote for each candidate in such group
but may not cast a vote for only one of the candidates in such group
forbids: Casting a vote for only one of the candidates in such group

review.title: Governor's executive reorganization plans
review.plain: The governor may present reorganization plans for executive agencies to the general court; a committee holds a hearing and reports, and a plan has the force of law after sixty days unless disapproved by a majority of either branch. Plans cannot be amended during those sixty days.
powers: the governor may prepare one or more reorganization plans
such reorganization plan shall have the force of law upon expiration of the sixty calendar days next following its presentation by the governor to the general court
limits: no such reorganization plan shall be subject to amendment by the general court before expiration of such sixty days

provisions.what: For the purpose of transferring, abolishing, consolidating or co-ordinating the whole or any part of any agency, or the functions thereof, within the executive department of the government of the commonwealth, or for the purpose of authorizing any officer of any agency within the executive department to delegate any of his functions, the governor may prepare one or more reorganization plans, each bearing an identifying number and may present such plan or plans to the general court, together with a message in explanation thereof

Every such reorganization plan shall be referred to an appropriate committee, to be determined by the Clerks of the Senate and the House of Representatives, with the approval of the President and Speaker, which committee shall not later than thirty days after the date of the Governor's presentation of said plan hold a public hearing thereon and shall not later than ten days after such hearing report that it approves or disapproves such plan
requires: hold a public hearing thereon
report that it approves or disapproves such plan

provisions.what: such reorganization plan shall have the force of law upon expiration of the sixty calendar days next following its presentation by the governor to the general court, unless disapproved by a majority vote of the members of either of the two branches of the general court present and voting, the general court not having been prorogued within such sixty days
conditions: the general court not having been prorogued within such sixty days
exceptions: unless disapproved by a majority vote of the members of either of the two branches of the general court present and voting

provisions.what: After its presentation by the governor to the general court, no such reorganization plan shall be subject to amendment by the general court before expiration of such sixty days
forbids: Amendment of a reorganization plan by the general court before expiration of such sixty days

provisions.what: Any such reorganization plan may provide for its taking effect on any date after expiration of such sixty days

every such reorganization plan shall comply with such conditions as the general court may from time to time prescribe by statute regarding the civil service status, seniority, retirement and other rights of any employee to be affected by such plan
requires: comply with such conditions as the general court may from time to time prescribe by statute

review.title: Industrial development of cities and towns
review.plain: The industrial development of cities and towns is a public function, and the commonwealth and its cities and towns may provide for it in the manner the general court determines.
powers: the commonwealth and the cities and towns therein may provide for the same

provisions.what: The industrial development of cities and towns is a public function
the commonwealth and the cities and towns therein may provide for the same in such manner as the general court may determine
provisions.holder: The commonwealth and the cities and towns therein
requires: in such manner as the general court may determine

review.title: Home rule for cities and towns
review.plain: Replaces Article II: grants the people of every city and town the right of self-government in local matters, sets how charters are adopted, revised and amended, lists powers not granted, and limits the general court to general laws or listed special laws. The bracketed words "ten months" were superseded.
rights: the right of self-government in local matters
powers: Any city or town shall have the power to adopt or revise a charter or to amend its existing charter
exercise any power or function which the general court has power to confer upon it
The general court shall have the power to act in relation to cities and towns
limits: No town of fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants shall adopt a city form of government
Nothing in this article shall be deemed to grant to any city or town the power to
but only by general laws which apply alike to all cities or to all towns, or to all cities and towns, or to a class of not fewer than two

provisions.what: Article II of the Articles of Amendment to the Constitution of the Commonwealth, as amended by Article LXX of said Articles of Amendment, is hereby annulled and the following is dopted in place thereof

It is the intention of this article to reaffirm the customary and traditional liberties of the people with respect to the conduct of their local government, and to grant and confirm to the people of every city and town the right of self-government in local matters, subject to the provisions of this article and to such standards and requirements as the general court may establish by law in accordance with the provisions of this article
provisions.holder: The people of every city and town
conditions: subject to the provisions of this article and to such standards and requirements as the general court may establish by law in accordance with the provisions of this article

provisions.what: Any city or town shall have the power to adopt or revise a charter or to amend its existing charter through the procedures set forth in sections three and four
requires: through the procedures set forth in sections three and four

provisions.what: The provisions of any adopted or revised charter or any charter amendment shall not be inconsistent with the constitution or any laws enacted by the general court in conformity with the powers reserved to the general court by section eight
forbids: Charter provisions inconsistent with the constitution or any laws enacted by the general court in conformity with the powers reserved to the general court by section eight

provisions.what: No town of fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants shall adopt a city form of government, and no town of fewer than six thousand inhabitants shall adopt a form of government providing for a town meeting limited to such inhabitants of the town as may be elected to meet, deliberate, act and vote in the exercise of the corporate powers of the town
forbids: A town of fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants adopting a city form of government
A town of fewer than six thousand inhabitants adopting a form of government providing for a town meeting limited to such inhabitants of the town as may be elected

provisions.what: Every city and town shall have the power to adopt or revise a charter in the following manner: A petition for the adoption or revision of a charter shall be signed by at least fifteen per cent of the number of legal voters residing in such city or town at the preceding state election
requires: signed by at least fifteen per cent of the number of legal voters residing in such city or town at the preceding state election

provisions.what: Whenever such a petition is filed with the board of registrars of voters of any city or town, the board shall within ten days of its receipt determine the sufficiency and validity of the signatures and certify the results to the city council of the city or board of selectmen of the town
provisions.binds: The board of registrars of voters
requires: determine the sufficiency and validity of the signatures
certify the results
terms: "board of registrars of voters": shall include any local authority of different designation which performs the duties of such registrars
"city council of the city or board of selectmen of the town": shall include local authorities of different designation performing the duties of such council or board

provisions.what: Objections to the sufficiency and validity of the signatures on any such petition as certified by the board of registrars of voters shall be made in the same manner as provided by law for objections to nominations for city or town offices

Within thirty days of receipt of certification of the board of registrars of voters that a petition contains sufficient valid signatures, the city council of the city or board of selectmen of the town shall by order provide for submitting to the voters of the city or town the question of adopting or revising a charter, and for the nomination and election of a charter commission
provisions.binds: The city council of the city or board of selectmen of the town

provisions.what: If the city or town has not previously adopted a charter pursuant to this section, the question submitted to the voters shall be: "Shall a commission be elected to frame a charter for (name of city or town)?" If the city or town has previously adopted a charter pursuant to this section, the question submitted to the voters shall be: "Shall a commission be elected to revise the charter of (name of city or town)?"

The charter commission shall consist of nine voters of the city or town, who shall be elected at large without party or political designation at the city or town election next held at least sixty days after the order of the city council of the city or board of selectmen of the town. The names of candidates for such commission shall be listed alphabetically on the ballot used at such election. Each voter may vote for nine candidates

The vote on the question submitted and the election of the charter commission shall take place at the same time. If the vote on the question submitted is in the affirmative, the nine candidates receiving the highest number of votes shall be declared elected

Within [ten months] after the election of the members of the charter commission, said commission shall submit the charter or revised charter to the city council of the city or the board of selectmen of the town, and such council or board shall provide for publication of the charter and for its submission to the voters of the city or town at the next city or town election held at least two months after such submission by the charter commission
provisions.binds: The charter commission; the city council or board of selectmen

provisions.what: If the charter or revised charter is approved by a majority of the voters of the city or town voting thereon, it shall become effective upon the date fixed in the charter
conditions: If the charter or revised charter is approved by a majority of the voters of the city or town voting thereon

provisions.what: Every city and town shall have the power to amend its charter in the following manner: The legislative body of a city or town may, by a two-thirds vote, propose amendments to the charter of the city or town
provisions.holder: The legislative body of a city or town
requires: a two-thirds vote
conditions: amendments of a city charter may be proposed only with the concurrence of the mayor in every city that has a mayor

any change in a charter relating in any way to the composition, mode of election or appointment, or terms of office of the legislative body, the mayor or city manager or the board of selectmen or town manager shall be made only by the procedure of charter revision set forth in section three

provisions.what: All proposed charter amendments shall be published and submitted for approval in the same manner as provided for adoption or revision of a charter

Duplicate certificates shall be prepared setting forth any charter that has been adopted or revised and any charter amendments approved, and shall be signed by the city or town clerk. One such certificate shall be deposited in the office of the secretary of the commonwealth and the other shall be recorded in the records of the city or town and deposited among its archives
All courts may take judicial notice of charters and charter amendments of cities and towns

Any city or town may, by the adoption, amendment, or repeal of local ordinances or by-laws, exercise any power or function which the general court has power to confer upon it, which is not inconsistent with the constitution or laws enacted by the general court in conformity with powers reserved to the general court in conformity with powers reserved to the general court by section eight, and which is not denied, either expressly or by clear implication, to the city or town by its charter
conditions: which is not inconsistent with the constitution or laws enacted by the general court
which is not denied, either expressly or by clear implication, to the city or town by its charter

provisions.what: This section shall apply to every city and town, whether or not it has adopted a charter pursuant to section three

Nothing in this article shall be deemed to grant to any city or town the power to (1) regulate elections other than those prescribed by sections three and four; (2) to levy, assess and collect taxes; (3) to borrow money or pledge the credit of the city or town; (4) to dispose of park land; (5) to enact private or civil law governing civil relationships except as an incident to an exercise of an independent municipal power; or (6) to define and provide for the punishment of a felony or to impose imprisonment as a punishment for any violation of law
exceptions: the foregoing enumerated powers may be granted by the general court in conformity with the constitution and with the powers reserved to the general court by section eight

provisions.what: nor shall the provisions of this article be deemed to diminish the powers of the judicial department of the commonwealth

The general court shall have the power to act in relation to cities and towns, but only by general laws which apply alike to all cities or to all towns, or to all cities and towns, or to a class of not fewer than two, and by special laws enacted (1) on petition filed or approved by the voters of a city or town, or the mayor and city council, or other legislative body, of a city, or the town meeting of a town, with respect to a law relating to that city or town; (2) by a two-thirds vote of each branch of the general court following a recommendation by the governor; (3) to erect and constitute metropolitan or regional entities, embracing any two or more cities or towns or cities and towns, or established with other than existing city or town boundaries, for any general or special public purpose or purposes, and to grant to these entities such powers, privileges and immunities as the general court shall deem necessary or expedient for the regulation and government thereof; or (4) solely for the incorporation or dissolution of cities or towns as corporate entities, alteration of city or town boundaries, and merger or consolidation of cities and towns, or any of these matters

Subject to the foregoing requirements, the general court may provide optional plans of city or town organization and government under which an optional plan may be adopted or abandoned by majority vote of the voters of the city or town voting thereon at a city or town election

no town of fewer than twelve thousand inhabitants may be authorized to adopt a city form of government, and no town of fewer than six thousand inhabitants may be authorized to adopt a form of town government providing for town meeting limited to such inhabitants of the town as may be elected to meet, deliberate, act and vote in the exercise of the corporate powers of the town
This section shall apply to every city and town whether or not it has adopted a charter pursuant to section three

All special laws relating to individual cities or towns shall remain in effect and have the force of an existing city or town charter, but shall be subject to amendment or repeal through the adoption, revision or amendment of a charter by a city or town in accordance with the provisions of sections three and four and shall be subject to amendment or repeal by laws enacted by the general court in conformity with the powers reserved to the general court by section eight

review.title: Governor's ten days to act on bills
review.plain: Amends four articles to give the governor ten days: an unreturned bill or resolve becomes law; a pocket veto applies if the general court adjourns within ten days; the governor may return a bill recommending amendment once; and item vetoes or reductions in appropriation bills must be explained within ten days.
powers: shall have the right to return it to the branch of the general court in which it originated with a recommendation that any amendment or amendments specified by him be made therein
The governor may disapprove or reduce items or parts of items in any bill appropriating money
limits: he shall have no right to return the same a second time with a recommendation to amend

provisions.what: Article II of section I of Chapter I of Part the Second of the constitution is hereby amended by striking out the second paragraph and inserting in place thereof the following paragraph
if any bill or resolve shall not be returned by the governor within ten days after it shall have been presented, the same shall have the force of a law
conditions: if any bill or resolve shall not be returned by the governor within ten days after it shall have been presented

provisions.what: Article I of the Articles of Amendment to the Constitution is hereby annulled and the following is adopted in place thereof

If any bill or resolve shall be objected to, and not approved by the governor, and if the general court shall adjourn within ten days after the same shall have been laid before the governor for his approbation, and thereby prevent his returning it with his objections, such bill or resolve shall not become a law, nor have force as such
conditions: if the general court shall adjourn within ten days after the same shall have been laid before the governor for his approbation, and thereby prevent his returning it with his objections

provisions.what: Article LVI of the Articles of the Articles of Amendments to the Constitution is hereby annulled and the following is adopted in place thereof

The governor, within ten days after any bill or resolve shall have been laid before him, shall have the right to return it to the branch of the general court in which it originated with a recommendation that any amendment or amendments specified by him be made therein. Such bill or resolve shall thereupon be before the general court and subject to amendment and re-enactment
conditions: within ten days after any bill or resolve shall have been laid before him

provisions.what: If such bill or resolve is re-enacted in any form it shall again be laid before the governor for his action, but he shall have no right to return the same a second time with a recommendation to amend
requires: it shall again be laid before the governor for his action
forbids: Returning the same a second time with a recommendation to amend

provisions.what: Article LXIII of the Articles of Amendment to the Constitution is hereby amended by striking out Section 5 and inserting in place thereof the following section
The governor may disapprove or reduce items or parts of items in any bill appropriating money. So much of such bill as he approves shall upon his signing the same become law

As to each item disapproved or reduced he shall transmit to the house in which the bill originated his reason for such disapproval or reduction, and the procedure shall then be the same as in the case of a bill disapproved as a whole
requires: transmit to the house in which the bill originated his reason for such disapproval or reduction

provisions.what: In case he shall fail so to transmit his reasons for such disapproval or reduction within ten days after the bill shall have been presented to him, such items shall have the force of law unless the general court by adjournment shall prevent such transmission, in which case they shall not be law
conditions: In case he shall fail so to transmit his reasons for such disapproval or reduction within ten days after the bill shall have been presented to him
exceptions: unless the general court by adjournment shall prevent such transmission, in which case they shall not be law

review.title: Governor's inability and vacancy
review.plain: The office of governor is deemed vacant when the governor, or the chief justice and a majority of the associate justices (or another body the general court provides), declares in writing that the governor is unable to discharge the office; it sets how the governor resumes, how the general court decides disputes, and when a special election is held.
powers: Thereupon the general court shall decide the issue

provisions.what: Whenever the governor transmits to the president of the senate and the speaker of the house his written declaration that he is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the office of governor shall be deemed to be vacant within the meaning of this Constitution

Whenever the chief justice and a majority of the associate justices of the supreme judicial court, or such other body as the general court may by law provide, transmit to the president of the senate and the speaker of the house their written declaration that the governor is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the office of governor shall be deemed to be vacant within the meaning of this Constitution

whenever the governor transmits to the president of the senate and the speaker of the house his written declaration that no inability exists such vacancy shall be deemed to have terminated four days thereafter and the governor shall resume the powers and duties of his office unless the chief justice and a majority of the associate justices of the supreme judicial court, or such other body as the general court may by law provide, transmit within said four days to the president of the senate and the speaker of the house their written declaration that the governor is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office
exceptions: unless the chief justice and a majority of the associate justices of the supreme judicial court, or such other body as the general court may by law provide, transmit within said four days ... their written declaration that the governor is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office

provisions.what: Thereupon the general court shall decide the issue, assembling within forty-eight hours for that purpose if not in session
requires: assembling within forty-eight hours for that purpose if not in session

provisions.what: If the general court within twenty-one days after receipt of the latter written declaration, or, if the general court is not in session, within twenty-one days after the general court is required to assemble, determine by a vote, taken by yeas and nays, of two thirds of each house present and voting thereon, that the governor is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office, the office of governor shall continue to be deemed to be vacant; otherwise such vacancy shall be deemed to have terminated and the governor shall resume the powers and duties of his office
requires: a vote, taken by yeas and nays, of two thirds of each house present and voting thereon

provisions.what: If a vacancy in the office of governor, as described in this Article, continues for six months and if such six-month period expires more than five months prior to a biennial state election other than an election for governor, there shall be an election of governor at such biennial state election for the balance of the unexpired four-year term
conditions: If a vacancy in the office of governor, as described in this Article, continues for six months and if such six-month period expires more than five months prior to a biennial state election other than an election for governor

review.title: Census and 240 representative districts
review.plain: Annulled: It provided a census every tenth year from 1971 as the basis for two hundred and forty representative districts and forty senatorial and councillor districts, and annulled Articles XXI and XXII as appearing in Article LXXI. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CI.

provisions.what: In the year nineteen hundred and seventy-one and every tenth year thereafter a census of the inhabitants of each city and town shall be taken. Said census shall be the basis for determining the representative districts for the ten year period beginning with the first Wednesday in the fourth January following the taking of said census
exceptions: such districts as established in the year nineteen hundred and sixty-eight shall continue until the first Wednesday in January in the year nineteen hundred and seventy-five

provisions.what: The house of representatives shall consist of two hundred and forty members. The general court shall, at its first regular session after the year in which said census was taken, divide the commonwealth into two hundred and forty representative districts of contiguous territory so that each representative will represent an equal number of inhabitants, as nearly as may be
requires: such districts shall be formed, as nearly as may be, without uniting two counties or parts of two or more counties, two towns or parts of two or more towns, two cities or parts of two or more cities, or a city and a town, or parts of cities and towns, into one district
the county of Dukes county and Nantucket county shall each be a representative district
no town containing less than six thousand inhabitants according to said census shall be divided

provisions.what: The general court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted calling in question any such division

Every representative, for one year at least immediately preceding his election, shall have been an inhabitant of the district for which he is chosen, and shall cease to represent such district when he shall cease to be an inhabitant of the commonwealth. The manner of calling and conducting the elections for the choice of representatives, and of ascertaining their election, shall be prescribed by law

Each census of inhabitants required in section one shall likewise be the basis for determining the senatorial districts and also the councillor districts. The senate shall consist of forty members. The general court shall, at its first regular session after the year in which said census is taken, divide the commonwealth into forty districts of contiguous territory, each district to contain, as nearly as may be, an equal number of inhabitants according to said census
requires: such districts shall be formed, as nearly as may be, without uniting two counties, or parts of two or more counties into one district
exceptions: such districts as established prior to the year nineteen hundred and seventy-one shall continue until the first Wednesday in January in the year nineteen hundred and seventy-five

provisions.what: The general court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted calling in question such division

Each district shall elect one senator, who shall have been an inhabitant of this commonwealth five years at least immediately preceding his election, and at the time of his election shall be an inhabitant of the district for which he is chosen; and he shall cease to represent such senatorial district when he shall cease to be an inhabitant of the commonwealth
Articles XXI and XXII of the Amendments to the Constitution, as appearing in Article LXXI of said Amendments, are hereby annulled

review.title: Striking a one-year residence requirement
review.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the words "within the commonwealth one year, and".

provisions.what: Article III of the Amendments to the Constitution, as amended, is hereby further amended by striking out the words "within the commonwealth one year, and"

review.title: Changing "twenty-one" to "nineteen" in Article III
review.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the word "twenty-one" and inserting in its place the word "nineteen".

provisions.what: Article III of the amendments to the Constitution, as amended, is hereby further amended by striking out the word "twenty-one" and inserting in place thereof the word: -- nineteen

review.title: Striking "pauper and" from Article III
review.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the words "pauper and".

provisions.what: Article III of the Amendments to the Constitution, as amended, is hereby further amended by striking out the words "pauper and"

review.title: State loans for higher education
review.plain: The general court has power to authorize the commonwealth to make loans, on terms it deems reasonable, to residents of the commonwealth for tuition and board at any college, university or other institution of higher learning.
powers: The general court shall have power to authorize the commonwealth to make loans

provisions.what: The general court shall have power to authorize the commonwealth to make loans, on such terms as it may deem reasonable, to any residents of the commonwealth for tuition and board at any college, university or other institution of higher learning

review.title: Right to clean air, water and environment
review.plain: Replaces Article XLIX: the people have the right to clean air and water, freedom from excessive noise, and the natural, scenic, historic and esthetic qualities of their environment; the general court may protect these rights and take lands, which may be put to other uses only by a two-thirds vote.
rights: The people shall have the right to clean air and water, freedom from excessive and unnecessary noise, and the natural, scenic, historic, and esthetic qualities of their environment
powers: The general court shall have the power to enact legislation necessary or expedient to protect such rights
the general court shall have the power to provide for the taking, upon payment of just compensation therefor
limits: shall not be used for other purposes or otherwise disposed of except by laws enacted by a two thirds vote

provisions.what: Article XLIX of the Amendments to the Constitution is hereby annulled and the following is adopted in place thereof
The people shall have the right to clean air and water, freedom from excessive and unnecessary noise, and the natural, scenic, historic, and esthetic qualities of their environment

the protection of the people in their right to the conservation, development and utilization of the agricultural, mineral, forest, water, air and other natural resources is hereby declared to be a public purpose
The general court shall have the power to enact legislation necessary or expedient to protect such rights

the general court shall have the power to provide for the taking, upon payment of just compensation therefor, or for the acquisition by purchase or otherwise, of lands and easements or such other interests therein as may be deemed necessary to accomplish these purposes
requires: payment of just compensation therefor

provisions.what: Lands and easements taken or acquired for such purposes shall not be used for other purposes or otherwise disposed of except by laws enacted by a two thirds vote, taken by yeas and nays, of each branch of the general court
forbids: Using lands and easements taken or acquired for such purposes for other purposes or otherwise disposing of them
exceptions: except by laws enacted by a two thirds vote, taken by yeas and nays, of each branch of the general court

review.title: Tenure and retirement of judges
review.plain: Replaces Article I of Chapter III: judicial officers hold office during good behavior; the governor, with the council's consent, may remove them on address of both houses or retire them for advanced age or disability after notice and hearing; judges shall be retired at seventy.
powers: the governor, with the consent of the council, may remove them upon the address of both houses of the legislature
the governor, with the consent of the council, may after due notice and hearing retire them

provisions.what: Article I of Chapter III of Part the Second of the Constitution , as amended by Article LVIII of the Amendments to the Constitution, is hereby annulled and the following Article is adopted in place thereof
The tenure, that all commissioned officers shall by law have in their offices, shall be expressed in their respective commissions
All judicial officers, duly appointed, commissioned and sworn, shall hold their offices during good behavior
exceptions: excepting such concerning whom there is different provision made in this Constitution

provisions.what: the governor, with the consent of the council, may remove them upon the address of both houses of the legislature
provisions.holder: The governor, with the consent of the council
requires: the consent of the council
the address of both houses of the legislature

provisions.what: the governor, with the consent of the council, may after due notice and hearing retire them because of advanced age or mental or physical disability
provisions.holder: The governor, with the consent of the council
requires: due notice and hearing

provisions.what: upon attaining seventy years of age said judges shall be retired. Such retirement shall be subject to any provisions made by law as to pensions or allowances payable to such officers upon their voluntary retirement

review.title: Taxing farm land by its agricultural use
review.plain: The general court may prescribe that agricultural or horticultural lands be valued for taxation by their agricultural or horticultural uses, but no parcel under five acres, or not actively so used for the two preceding years, shall be valued at less than fair market value.
powers: Full power and authority are hereby given and granted to the general court to prescribe
limits: shall be valued at less than fair market value under this article

provisions.what: Full power and authority are hereby given and granted to the general court to prescribe, for the purpose of developing and conserving agricultural or horticultural lands, that such lands shall be valued, for the purpose of taxation, according to their agricultural or horticultural uses

no parcel of land which is less than five acres in area or which has not been actively devoted to agricultural or horticultural uses for the two years preceding the tax year shall be valued at less than fair market value under this article
forbids: Valuing at less than fair market value a parcel of land which is less than five acres in area or which has not been actively devoted to agricultural or horticultural uses for the two years preceding the tax year

review.title: Voting age changed to eighteen
review.plain: Further amends Article III of the Amendments by striking out the word giving the age at which a citizen has a right to vote for Governor and other public officers and inserting the word "eighteen".

provisions.what: Article III of the Amendments to the Constitution, as amended, is hereby further amended by striking out the word indicating the age at which a citizen shall have a right to vote in an election of Governor and other public officers and inserting in place thereof the following word: -- eighteen

review.title: 160 representative districts and 40 senate districts
review.plain: The house has one hundred and sixty members and the senate forty, in districts of contiguous territory with equal numbers of inhabitants as nearly as may be; voters may petition the supreme judicial court about districts, and Article XCII is annulled. Bracketed census wording was superseded.
powers: Original jurisdiction is hereby vested in the supreme judicial court
The General Court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted
limits: no town containing less than twenty-five hundred inhabitants according to said census shall be divided

provisions.what: In the year nineteen hundred and seventy-five and every tenth year thereafter a census of the inhabitants of each city and town shall be taken. Said census shall be the basis for determining the representative districts for the ten year period beginning with the first Wednesday in the fourth January following the taking of said census

The House of Representatives shall consist of one hundred and sixty members. The General Court shall, at its first regular session after the year in which said census was taken, divide the Commonwealth into one hundred and sixty representative districts of contiguous territory so that each representative will represent an equal number of inhabitants, as nearly as may be
requires: such districts shall be formed, as nearly as may be, without uniting two counties or parts of two or more counties, two towns or parts of two or more towns, two cities or parts of two or more cities, or a city and a town, or parts of cities and towns, into one district
forbids: no town containing less than twenty-five hundred inhabitants according to said census shall be divided

provisions.what: The General Court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted calling in question any such division

Every representative, for one year at least immediately preceding his election, shall have been an inhabitant of the district for which he is chosen and shall cease to represent such district when he shall cease to be an inhabitant of the Commonwealth. The manner of calling and conducting the elections for the choice of representatives, and of ascertaining their election, shall be prescribed by law

The Senate shall consist of forty members. The General Court shall, at its first regular session after the year in which said census is taken, divide the Commonwealth into forty districts of contiguous territory, each district to contain, as nearly as may be, an equal number of inhabitants according to said census
requires: such districts shall be formed, as nearly as may be, without uniting two counties, or parts of two or more counties, into one district

provisions.what: The General Court may by law limit the time within which judicial proceedings may be instituted calling in question such division

Each district shall elect one senator, who shall have been an inhabitant of this Commonwealth five years at least immediately preceding his election and at the time of his election shall be an inhabitant of the district for which he is chosen; and he shall cease to represent such senatorial district when he shall cease to be an inhabitant of the Commonwealth. The manner of calling and conducting the elections for the choice of senators and councillors, and of ascertaining their election, shall be prescribed by law

Original jurisdiction is hereby vested in the supreme judicial court upon the petition of any voter of the Commonwealth, filed with the clerk of the supreme judicial court for the Commonwealth, for judicial relief relative to the establishment of House of Representatives, councillor and senatorial districts
provisions.holder: The supreme judicial court; any voter of the Commonwealth

provisions.what: Article XCII of the Amendments to the Constitution is hereby annulled

review.title: Legislative recesses
review.plain: Replaces Article LII: the General Court, by concurrent vote of the two houses, may take a recess or recesses amounting to not more than thirty days.
powers: may take a recess or recesses
limits: amounting to not more than thirty days

provisions.what: Article LII of the Articles of Amendment to the Constitution is hereby annulled and the following is adopted in place thereof
The General Court, by concurrent vote of the two houses, may take a recess or recesses amounting to not more than thirty days
requires: concurrent vote of the two houses
forbids: Recesses amounting to more than thirty days

review.title: No public money for private or religious institutions
review.plain: Replaces Section 2 of Article XLVI: no public money, property or credit may aid any institution, school or undertaking not publicly owned and controlled, or any church or religious society, with listed exceptions; grants-in-aid to private higher educational institutions or their students are allowed.
limits: No grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of credit shall be made or authorized

no such grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of public credit shall be made or authorized for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any church, religious denomination or society

provisions.what: Article XLVI of the Articles of Amendment to the Constitution of the Commonwealth is hereby amended by striking out section 2 and inserting in place thereof the following section

No grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of credit shall be made or authorized by the Commonwealth or any political subdivision thereof for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any infirmary, hospital, institution, primary or secondary school, or charitable or religious undertaking which is not publicly owned and under the exclusive control, order and supervision of public officers or public agents authorized by the Commonwealth or federal authority or both
provisions.binds: The Commonwealth or any political subdivision thereof
forbids: Grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of credit for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any infirmary, hospital, institution, primary or secondary school, or charitable or religious undertaking which is not publicly owned
exceptions: appropriations may be made for the maintenance and support of the Soldiers' Home in Massachusetts and for free public libraries in any city or town and to carry out legal obligations, if any, already entered into

provisions.what: no such grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of public credit shall be made or authorized for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any church, religious denomination or society
provisions.binds: The Commonwealth or any political subdivision thereof
forbids: Grant, appropriation or use of public money or property or loan of public credit for the purpose of founding, maintaining or aiding any church, religious denomination or society

provisions.what: Nothing herein contained shall be construed to prevent the Commonwealth from making grants-in-aid to private higher educational institutions or to students or parents or guardians of students attending such institutions
